comment: Differences from the oracle that are understood and not yet fixed. Each entry pins the exact number of failing cases per target; run_diff.py fails on any failure no entry explains and on any count that changed (a fix must update this file). ps3recomp commit: 39a36296. Each entry's 'rpcs3' field records what RPCS3's interpreter does (run_rpcs3_oracle.py).

entries.note: FPSCR[RN] other than round-to-nearest is ignored by fadd/fmul/fdiv/fadds/fmuls/fmadd/frsp/fctiw/fctid/fcfid: results are always rounded to nearest. Games normally keep the PS3 default (nearest); check the game for mtfsf/mtfsfi before relying on this.
entries.rpcs3: RPCS3 interpreter (26098fb42, accuracy options on) also ignores RN: same result as the lifted code in all 56 cases.

entries.note: fsqrt of a negative number or -inf returns the host's default NaN. x86 produces 0xfff8... (negative), PowerPC 0x7ff8.... arm64's default NaN is already 0x7ff8..., so the Android target matches.
entries.rpcs3: RPCS3 on x86 also returns 0xfff8... here (it uses the host's NaN).

entries.note: lfs of a single-precision signalling NaN sets the quiet bit (host float->double conversion). The ISA converts without quieting.
entries.rpcs3: RPCS3 interpreter quiets the sNaN too (same as the lifted code).

entries.note: stfs converts with a C (float) cast, which rounds, overflows to inf and quiets sNaN. The ISA store conversion takes FRS[0:1] || FRS[5:34] (truncation) for values outside single range and NaNs. Values already rounded to single (frsp, single ops) are unaffected.
entries.rpcs3: RPCS3 interpreter rounds too (same as the lifted code).

entries.note: A lane whose input is a signalling NaN returns the default NaN 0x7fc00000; the oracle returns the quieted input (0x7fc00001), keeping the payload.
entries.rpcs3: RPCS3 interpreter (Accurate Vector NaN Values on) also returns the default NaN (same as the lifted code).

entries.note: vctuxs of a value in (-1, 0) sets VSCR[SAT]; truncation gives 0, which is in range, so the oracle leaves SAT clear. The result vector itself matches.
entries.rpcs3: RPCS3 interpreter (Set Saturation Bit on) also sets SAT (same as the lifted code).

entries.note: With VSCR[NJ]=1 the vector float compares (vcmpeqfp/vcmpgefp/vcmpgtfp/vcmpbfp) compare denormal operands as they are. The Cell edition of the Vector/SIMD PEM (v2.07c, 2006-10-26), section 3.2.1.2 'Non-Java Mode', says denormalized input operands are flushed to a correctly signed zero before being used by the instruction; the vcmpbfp page repeats it for the comparison. qemu follows that. Confidence: high for vcmpbfp (explicit), medium-high for the other three (general rule). Not checked on Cell hardware.
entries.rpcs3: RPCS3 interpreter with 'PPU Accurate Non-Java Mode' on also does not flush here (same as the lifted code).
